question: What is meant by an "own goal" in football?

options.text: A goal scored by a goalkeeper
A goal scored from a penalty
A goal scored accidentally into one's own net
A goal scored during injury time

solution:
The correct answer is __**A goal scored accidentally into one's own net**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An "own goal" in football refers to a situation where a player inadvertently scores a goal in their own team's net.
 
• It typically occurs due to a mistake, misjudgment, or an attempt to clear the ball that results in the ball going into their own goal.
 
• Own goals are counted as valid scores but credited to the opposing team.
 
• These goals can significantly impact the outcome of a match, often leading to frustration for the player and the team.
 
• FIFA and other football governing bodies officially record own goals in match statistics, but they are not attributed to the player as a positive contribution to the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional __**

 
• Dribble: Running with the ball, keeping control with your feet.
 
• Pass: Kicking or moving the ball to a teammate.
 
• Tackle: Attempting to take the ball from an opponent legally.
 
• Shoot: Kicking the ball towards the opponent's goal.
 
• Header: Using the head to direct the ball.
 
• Volley: Kicking the ball in mid-air.
 
• Cross: A pass from the side of the field into the penalty area.
 
• Chip: A high, delicate kick over an opponent, usually the goalkeeper.
 
• Backheel: Kicking the ball backward with the heel.
